goal: Middle pane becomes a Ruby console: a persistent ruby process with stdin/stdout/stderr bound, multi-line entry decided by Ruby itself, clear success/error rendering, Ctrl-C to discard an entry or interrupt running code (second Ctrl-C kills and restarts a stuck process).

decisions.choice: Custom Vue console (no xterm.js); ANSI codes stripped
First Ctrl-C sends SIGINT to ruby's process group; a second Ctrl-C while still busy SIGKILLs it and starts a fresh ruby (definitions lost, said so on screen)
Up/Down recall entries when no file is open; with a file open they keep scrolling it

Ask the ruby process itself using IRB::RubyLex#check_code_state (the same logic irb uses): finished -> eval, unfinished -> continuation prompt, unrecoverable -> eval immediately so Ruby reports the SyntaxError
decisions.evidence: irblex_probe.out.txt (26/26 cases classified correctly) vs prism_probe.out.txt (raw Prism errors cannot tell '1 +' from '1 +* 2')

decisions.choice: User code keeps the real stdin/stdout/stderr pipes. Control messages (check/eval/results) travel over a separate Unix socket. After each eval the driver writes a nonce marker on stdout and stderr, and Rust releases the result only after both markers arrive, so output always appears before its result

criteria.measure: E2: locals, methods, classes survive; E20: driver's own locals are not visible

criteria.title: Multi-line entry is decided correctly
criteria.measure: 26 completeness cases (K1-K26) match IRB's verdicts; E3 multi-line def evaluates as one entry

criteria.title: Bad syntax is reported, session survives
criteria.measure: E4/E5: SyntaxError with Ruby's own message, next entry works

criteria.title: Runtime errors are readable
criteria.measure: E6: class + message, backtrace only (rls) frames with correct line; E18 inspect that raises still renders

criteria.title: Output is complete and ordered
criteria.measure: E7/E8/E21: all stdout/stderr bytes arrive before the result, UTF-8 intact, 200 KB in one entry

criteria.title: Ctrl-C interrupts running code, state kept
criteria.measure: E10-E13: interrupt latency < 1000 ms (2000 ms under an output flood); earlier variables still defined

criteria.title: Second Ctrl-C kills a stuck process
criteria.measure: E14: trap('INT'){} + loop survives first Ctrl-C, second kills; new session ready < 3000 ms

criteria.title: Process death is survivable
criteria.measure: E15-E17: exit, exit!(3), SIGKILL self -> reported with status, fresh session works; E23 missing ruby reported

criteria.title: Console behaviour (UI logic)
criteria.measure: bun tests C1-C10: prompts, continuation, Ctrl-C discard, stdin routing, history, paste, rendering kinds

criteria.title: Builds clean
criteria.measure: vue-tsc, vite build, cargo build, cargo test, bun test all exit 0 (run-checks.sh)

attempts.title: Probe: how to tell an unfinished entry from a broken one
attempts.changed: No app code. Ran two probes over 20-26 inputs: raw Prism error lists, and IRB::RubyLex#check_code_state.
attempts.result: Raw Prism: ambiguous ('1 +\n' and '1 +* 2' share expect_expression_after_operator; 'x = 1 \\' reports no error). IRB lexer: every case classified as irb would. Prism::ParseResult#continuable? does not exist in prism 1.5.3.
attempts.flag: Known irb quirk carried over on purpose: an error inside an open block ('def f / 1 +* 2') keeps asking for more lines until 'end' or Ctrl-C.
attempts.next: Build driver.rb + Rust session with real-ruby scenario tests (E1-E23, K1-K26).

attempts.title: Backend: driver.rb + Rust session + 49 real-ruby scenarios
attempts.changed: Added src-tauri/ruby/driver.rb (eval loop, IRB completeness check, nonce markers), src-tauri/src/ruby.rs (process group, Unix control socket, ordered event stream, interrupt/kill/restart), 5 Tauri commands, tests/ruby_session.rs, run-checks.sh.
attempts.result: 6/6 gates green; 49/49 scenarios (K01-K26, E01-E23) pass on 3 consecutive runs. Interrupt latency ~70 ms against limits of 1000/2000 ms.
attempts.flag: E13 (Ctrl-C under an output flood) failed at first. The cause was the test harness, not the session: it rescanned every collected event before each receive (O(n^2) over about 100k events). The Result really arrived about 300 ms after Ctrl-C. Fixed in the harness, and no limit was loosened. Lead review then found 4 issues: kill(-0) could signal the app itself if pid were missing; LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 forced on the child; run-checks.sh uses GNU-only date; build-machine sysroot paths exported unconditionally.
attempts.next: Fix the 4 review findings, then build the Vue console (console.ts state machine + RubyConsole.vue) with bun tests C01-C10.

attempts.title: Frontend: console.ts state machine + RubyConsole.vue + review fixes from #1
attempts.changed: Fixed the 4 backend review findings (pid guard, UTF-8 set inside driver.rb instead of forcing LC_ALL, portable timing + guarded sysroot in run-checks.sh). Added src/console.ts, src/components/RubyConsole.vue, console mounted as the base layer of the middle pane, document-level Ctrl-C forwarding, tests/console.test.ts (C01-C12).
attempts.result: 6/6 gates, 61/61 scenarios. E21 (UTF-8) still passes with this machine locale = US-ASCII, so the driver-side encoding fix works without LC_ALL.
attempts.flag: Lead review found 2 UI bugs that the tests did not cover: (1) the running... hint never cleared after the first long eval; (2) pasting several lines into a program reading stdin stalled after the first line. Evidence bug too: C08 second case wrote to the same report id and overwrote the first.
attempts.next: Fix both bugs, add C13 regression test, give C08 paste-abort its own report id (C08b).
